name: Alert Dialog
description: A modal dialog that interrupts the user's workflow to communicate an important message and acquire a response, such as action confirmation prompts or error acknowledgments.

keyboard_interactions.action: Moves focus to next tabbable element inside the dialog; wraps from last to first
Moves focus to previous tabbable element inside the dialog; wraps from first to last

roles.description: Identifies the element as an alert dialog, enabling assistive technologies to give it special treatment

required_attributes.description: Provides accessible name, preferably referencing visible title
References the element containing the alert message text

notes: An alertdialog is a dialog-modal (see patterns/dialog-modal.md) with exactly two differences: role='alertdialog', and aria-describedby is REQUIRED rather than optional.
Use it only for an urgent interruption requiring a response — confirming a destructive action, or a failed operation. A normal form in a modal is a plain dialog.
aria-describedby is required: it points at the message text, which is announced immediately on open. Without it the user hears the title and nothing about what they are confirming.
Focus the LEAST destructive action: Cancel, not Delete. An Enter keypress in flight from the previous screen must not delete the account.
Do not use role='alertdialog' for a message with no decision — that is a live region (patterns/alert.md), which does not steal focus.
Everything from dialog-modal still applies: never open with the `open` attribute, always .showModal().

raweb_criteria.reason: role='alertdialog' plus an accessible name and description must be exposed.
Fully keyboard operable, exactly like a modal dialog.
It interrupts the user — it must follow a user action, never appear unprompted.
role='alertdialog' is announced like an alert on open: its description is read immediately, without waiting.
Focus must be visible on every control, including against the backdrop.
Focus enters on open and returns to the invoking element on close.
Escape and a visible cancel path keep the Tab loop legal.
